solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Politicians on track for election?

parts.note: the clue pictures politicians literally on a race track, but candidates standing for election are said to be running, and their partners on the ticket share the race

explanation.surface: A question about which politicians are well placed to win an upcoming vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On track' suggests progress towards a goal; read literally, people running together on a track are companions in the race, which is what a vice-presidential partner is.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates who stand together on one ticket, such as a presidential hopeful and deputy, are both politicians in the electoral race.

clue.text: A French chap accepting university application

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the chap word holds the university letter

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is admitted to university after sending in his form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application' suggests a form for university; it is something applied to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment or salve is something rubbed on, so it is an application in the medical sense.

clue.text: Need a tip off when there's little difference, in the main

definitions.text: when there's little difference, in the main

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or not right, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gambler needs to drop a hint when the odds barely differ, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the sea, not 'mostly': this is a sea state with the smallest gap between high and low water.
explanation.definitionFit: Around the moon's quarters, the tidal range on the ocean is smallest, so high and low water differ little.

clue.text: Votes against hooter being sounded

indicators.note: being sounded means spoken out, so the word is replaced by one with the same pronunciation

parts.note: hooter is British slang for the nose

explanation.surface: A siren goes off when the motion is defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a horn or siren; it is British slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliament the members voting against a motion are counted as the negative side, opposite the ayes.

clue.text: Mad chemist at work, not given fair opposition

indicators.note: at work means busy operating on something, so the ten letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A crazed scientist in his laboratory faces an unfair contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest between unequal opponents is unfairly paired, so one side lacks fair competition.

clue.text: Fill time, with work increasing

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
up means rising or increasing, as in prices are up

explanation.surface: Pass the hours while the workload keeps growing.
explanation.definitionFit: A refill of a glass or tank, adding more to bring it to the brim, is a fill.

clue.text: Flyer's argument after fight

indicators.note: after places the argument word following the fight word

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice
a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: A pilot's dispute comes after a punch-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a pilot or leaflet; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown bird is a creature that takes to the air, so it is a flyer.

clue.text: Oliver, for example, is in charge of meeting for game

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage musical based on Oliver Twist
someone who chairs a meeting is in charge of it

explanation.surface: Oliver presides over a gathering to choose a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver looks like a person's name, but it is the hit stage show Oliver!.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's party pastime where players circle seats while music plays is a classic game.

clue.text: Worry people suppressed by Cortes fighting around north

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece suppressed by another sits beneath it, so the people word comes after
around means the shuffled letters go round the north letter
fighting suggests turmoil, so the letters of Cortes are scrambled

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A worrying tale: natives held down by the conquistador Cortés battling round the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Cortés is the Spanish conquistador; 'fighting' gives COSTER, 'around' makes CONSTER, and in a down clue 'suppressed by' means sitting underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm or dismay, a state of anxious shock, is a form of worry.

clue.text: Get better software at university level?

parts.note: a student who is up is in residence at university, a British usage
a grade is a level or rank

explanation.surface: A student wonders whether to buy improved software at university standard.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you are 'up' at university (Oxford or Cambridge especially) and 'go down' when you leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Installing a newer, improved version of a program is the standard computing verb for obtaining improved software.

clue.text: Singer's work organised by son, with love

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
ran, as in ran an event, means organised it
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A singer's composition was arranged by her son, with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work organised' reads as one phrase but gives two pieces, OP and RAN; 'by son' places S beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female voice in a choir gives its name to the vocalist who sings that part.

clue.text: Still at home? Finally leave after breakfast

parts.note: someone who is in is at home

indicators.note: finally applies to each of the three following words, taking the closing letter of every one

explanation.surface: Still in the house? You should finally head out once breakfast is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes the last letters of three words, leave, after and breakfast, giving E, R and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless and lacking any power to move is still, as in a lifeless, unmoving object.

clue.text: Lots in America complain about chest pains, ultimately

indicators.note: about means going around, so the complaining word and the closing letter are wrapped round the chest

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of the word pains

parts.note: an ark is an old word for a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Many Americans grumble about aches in the chest, in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' is a noun, not 'many': parking lots, the American term for places to leave cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call areas for parking vehicles parking lots, so lots there are the British equivalent.

clue.text: Acknowledgments from delegations after a day

indicators.note: after places the delegations word following the first two pieces

parts.note: missions are delegations sent abroad

explanation.surface: Confessions came from the diplomatic delegations a day later.
explanation.definitionFit: Confessions or concessions that something is true are things acknowledged, as in admissions of guilt.

clue.text: Outdid a tricky performance from person who taught himself

indicators.note: tricky suggests something twisted or intricate, so these seven letters are rearranged

parts.note: an act is a performance or turn on stage

explanation.surface: Someone outshone a difficult stage show by a self-taught performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no teacher who learned everything alone is self-taught, from the Greek for self and teaching.

clue.text: Cute women must be protected by supporter

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed inside it, so the women go within the supporter

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball before it is struck
W is the standard abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: Something sweet: women need to be guarded by someone backing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan or backer, but here it is the golf tee that holds up the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in a sickly, overly dainty sense is the British adjective for something affectedly quaint or sentimental.

clue.text: Temperature in red meat possibly was important

indicators.note: in places the temperature letter inside the reworked letters
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: How hot the inside of a steak was mattered to the chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges RED MEAT into MATERED; 'in' then sets T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being significant or of consequence in the past tense, as in it counted, means was important.

clue.text: Taxi crossing river might catch one!

indicators.note: crossing means placed across, so the taxi word is straddled over the river letter

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: Someone taking a cab over a river might snag a passenger, or a fare.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, to 'catch a crab' is to jam an oar in the water, a mishap of crossing a river; the exclamation mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers who mistime a stroke are said to catch a crab, so a crab is the thing such a rower catches.

clue.text: V is for victory, in a way

indicators.note: in places the victory word inside the other two pieces

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a gain is a win or victory

explanation.surface: The letter V stands for victory in some sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'V is for victory' is a wartime slogan; here V is short for versus, as in a fixture list.
explanation.definitionFit: V abbreviates versus, Latin for opposed to, as in Smith v Jones in law or sport.

clue.text: Animal painter men fancy

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the ten letters are decorated into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wildlife artists like to paint a fancy creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as a verb, men who fancy a painter, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-dwelling member of the weasel family found in British and European forests is a wild animal.

clue.text: Stress is rising in joint

indicators.note: in places the turned-up word inside the joint

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting part of a mortise-and-tenon joint in woodwork

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom up, so the word is turned around

explanation.surface: Pressure is mounting in a joint of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a knee or hip; it is the carpentry joint. 'Rising' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental or physical strain, as in nervous pressure, is stress.

clue.text: A weapon in catalogue spreading fear

indicators.note: in places the weapon inside the catalogue

parts.note: a list is a catalogue or inventory
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A gun listed in an arms catalogue causes panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises needless warnings stirs up panic, so the description fits anyone causing undue fear.

clue.text: Raising objective, admitting an obsession

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the turned word holds the next piece
in a down clue, raising means lifting from the bottom, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: an aim is an objective

explanation.surface: Pursuing a goal, while conceding a fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' suggests lifting a goal, but in a down entry it turns the word upwards to MIA, which 'admitting' then opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze or fixation, as in a passing fad for something, is a compulsive obsession.

clue.text: Belief that also comes from the east

indicators.text: that also comes from the east
indicators.note: read from the east, that is right to left, the word is unchanged, so the defined word reads the same both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A doctrine that originated in the Orient too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the east' sounds like an origin in Asia; in a grid, reading from the east means reading right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or doctrine held as true by a group is one of its core beliefs.

clue.text: A short note on end of the recess

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a short note added to a letter

indicators.note: end of picks the closing letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A brief message left at the back of the alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests music; here it is the PS at the foot of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular vaulted alcove at the east end of a church is an architectural recess.

clue.text: Race, enthusiastic about encounter

parts.note: to run is to race
someone into a hobby is enthusiastic about it

explanation.surface: A sprinter keen on meeting a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting someone by chance is the phrasal-verb idiom for an unexpected encounter.

clue.text: Wine firm providing cover for Independent series of columns

indicators.note: providing cover for means wrapping around, so the wine and firm enclose the independent

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A wine company sheltering a non-aligned politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' is capitalised to suggest the British newspaper, but it is just the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed porch with a row of pillars at a building's entrance is a classical colonnade.

clue.text: Unparalleled time, and managed track, including finish

parts.note: ran, as in ran a business, means managed

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the track word wraps the finish

parts.note: a scent is the trail or track a hound follows
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A record-breaking time from someone who handled the circuit right to the finish line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' suggests a racecourse, but it is the trail a hunting dog follows by smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surpassing all others, beyond ordinary limits, has no equal or parallel.
